title: Fruits highest in protein

seo.title: Fruits highest in protein
seo.meta_description: Guava, passion fruit and avocado are among the higher-protein fresh fruits, but even the leaders provide only about 2 to 3 grams per 100 grams. Fruit contributes protein; it is rarely a primary protein source.
seo.search_intent: Rank fresh fruits by protein per 100 grams and put the numbers in context against true protein foods.

excerpt: Among common fresh fruits, guava provides about 2.6 g protein per 100 g, passion fruit about 2.2 g and avocado about 2.0 g. Those are high within the fruit category but low compared with beans, dairy, eggs, fish or meat, so fruit usually adds protein rather than serving as the main source.
content_html:
Calling a fruit “high-protein” can make a small number sound bigger than it is. There are clear leaders within fruit, but fresh fruit as a category is low in protein. The top entries supply only around 2 to 3 grams per 100 grams.

Fresh fruit ranked per 100 grams

These values use USDA references for raw edible fruit. Dried fruit is kept out of the table because removing water concentrates protein, sugar and calories at the same time.

Fresh fruitProtein per 100 g
Guava2.55 g
Passion fruit2.20 g
Avocado2.00 g
Jackfruit1.72 g
Pomegranate1.67 g
Apricot1.40 g
Blackberries1.39 g
Raspberries1.20 g
Kiwi1.14 g
Banana1.09 g

Guava has more than twice the protein concentration of banana, but the absolute gap is only about 1.46 g per 100 g.

Guava wins the category, not the protein-food contest

A 150 g serving of guava contributes roughly 3.8 g protein. The same weight of avocado provides around 3 g and banana around 1.6 g.

For scale, 100 g cooked lentils provide roughly 9 g protein, while 100 g cooked chicken breast can exceed 30 g. Fruit can add to a day's total but usually cannot carry a high-protein meal.

Why dried fruit belongs in a separate comparison

Raisins, dried apricots and prunes show higher protein numbers per 100 g largely because water has been removed. The same process also concentrates sugars and calories. Mixing them with fresh fruit would make a water-loss effect look like a biological protein advantage.

Fruit has other jobs

Low protein is not a weakness. Depending on the fruit, you may be getting fiber, vitamin C, potassium, carotenoids and a wide range of plant compounds. Choosing guava over an orange only to gain a gram or two of protein misses most of the nutritional story.

How to use this ranking

If your goal is meaningfully higher protein, change the foods that can move the total: yogurt, eggs, beans, tofu, fish, meat, nuts or seeds. Fruit can accompany them and add roughly 1 to 4 grams depending on the fruit and serving.

faq.question: Which fresh fruit has the most protein?
faq.answer: Among common USDA entries, guava is a leader at about 2.55 g protein per 100 g.

faq.question: Is avocado high in protein?
faq.answer: It has about 2 g per 100 g, which is relatively high for fruit but low compared with foods normally used as protein sources.

faq.question: Does dried fruit have more protein?
faq.answer: It is more concentrated per 100 g because much of the water has been removed; sugars and calories concentrate too.
